Job Description:
About Shiftbase

We build workforce software that helps people get work done. More than 10,000 companies use our platform every month to plan shifts and track time, with less admin in the way.

We work from our Zoetermeer office with over 80 people and we grow every year. The culture is open and informal. You can push back on an idea regardless of title, and we change how we work when someone makes the case in retro.

About The Role

You build frontend features that customers use the day you release them. You sit in a product team with backend, QA, design and product, and you take a feature from a rough product idea to a screen a planner can use without a manual.

Your time is a balance between working on features, bugs and resolving technical debt.

Claude Code is how our engineers write software. Everyone here uses it daily, and whole features now go out with an agent doing most of the coding. You still own what you merge, so you read the diff, you know why it works, and you can defend it in review. The interesting part of the job is deciding what to hand to an agent, what to write yourself, and what context the agent needs to get it right the first time.

You ask what a planner is trying to do before you read what the ticket says. You automate the parts of your own process that don't need a human.

Year one, in order

First, ship. Deliver features in scheduling and time tracking. Start small, then take one full feature from the product conversation through to release.

Then, own an area. Pick up a product surface end to end and become the person the team asks about it, including what it should do next. That covers how AI fits your area, which patterns you document for the agent and which calls you keep for yourself.

Along the way, make what you build safe to change. Restructure and test the paths you build on while you build on them. Extend test coverage where it's lacking. We move fast and keep quality up by automating what a human doesn't need to do, including the checks that catch what an agent got wrong.

What You'll Do

Design and build frontend features starting from rough product ideas
Deliver features with Claude Code, from the prompt through to the pull request, and review the output as closely as a colleague's
Write the patterns, conventions and project context our agents work from, so generated frontend code lands in the right shape
Turn tangled domain rules into screens people can use without a manual
Fix bugs in your own features and in code you've never seen
Improve the code you touch while you touch it, so the next feature in that area costs less
Write and maintain automated tests in Jest and Playwright
Ship in short cycles with your product team
Pair, review, and teach what you know


How we work

Frontend in Angular, backend in PHP, a web app and a mobile app in React Native. Tests in Jest and Playwright. We develop AI-assisted with Claude Code as the primary tool, and a growing share of our code starts there. Human review and engineers owning what they ship keep it safe. We ship in short cycles in product teams with mixed specialisations. We pair often, with each other and with an agent open. Every quarter you get time to build and ship one of your own ideas, and we run hackathons.

Must-haves

3+ years of professional experience with an SPA framework, Angular preferred. Depth in React or Vue works if you can show you'll carry it over.

You ship. You've delivered features to real users at a steady pace, and you can tell us what you cut to get them out.

You've shipped production code with an AI agent. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar. Tell us where you let it run, where you took the keyboard back, and what you changed about your own workflow after a month of it.

You automate your tests. Jest and Playwright, or equivalents, and you have an opinion about what deserves a test.

You simplify. Hand you a tangled domain problem and you produce a screen that hides the tangle.

You explain your choices. In review, in a design discussion, and to a product manager who doesn't read code.

You work as a peer. You pair, you review, and you make the people around you better without needing a title to be heard.

Nice-to-haves

Claude Code in particular, or agent setups you've tuned for a team rather than yourself
TypeScript at depth
Storybook or component library ownership
React
TDD
PHP, or enough backend to reason about the API you're consuming
Familiarity with a complex, regulated domain (ours covers scheduling, time tracking, leave, and labour law across countries)


This might be your dream job if…

✅ You want your work in front of customers within days

✅ You'd rather own a feature end to end than take a finished spec

✅ You want a say in how a team writes frontend code with agents while the answer is still open

✅ You improve the code you touch without being asked, and you stop before it turns into a six-week rewrite

✅ You like a domain that takes months to learn

This probably isn't your dream job if…

⛔️ You want the technical approach decided before the ticket reaches you

⛔️ You want a job where AI stays out of your editor

⛔️ You'd merge agent output you can't explain in review

⛔️ You'd stop shipping to finish a refactor

⛔️ You prefer pixel work and would rather leave tests and architecture to someone else

⛔️ You'd rather work alone than pair and review

What We Offer

A laptop on Mac, Windows, or Linux
32 or 40 hours workweek 
Hybrid, from home or the Zoetermeer office
25 vacation days based on a 40-hour contract
Pension plan
NS business card or travel expenses reimbursed. 
Training budget for personal development


Please be aware that this is not a remote position and we are not taking applications in consideration outside of the Netherlands for this position.

Working closely with the Lead for Digital Support Strategy, you will turn partner friction points into scalable self-service solutions across key touchpoints.

Data analysis: Use web, search, and survey analytics to derive actionable insights that refine digital support touchpoints.

Proactive personalization campaigns: Plan, build, and execute targeted web banner use cases on Partner Hub and triggered email journeys via Salesforce Marketing Cloud. Content strategy and briefing expertise: Deep understanding of how digital content functions to drive user action, task completion, and findability. Proven ability to audit content ecosystems, translate data into actionable briefs, and direct content writers effectively. AI knowledge and output optimization: Practical experience using Generative AI technologies and a clear understanding of how LLMs consume information (including RAG frameworks). Ability to leverage continuous feedback loops to evaluate and improve GenAI-powered output from conversational interfaces.
Data and analytics: Demonstrated ability to draw actionable insights from qualitative feedback and analytics using tools like Google Analytics, Tableau, Qualtrics, and Snowflake (or equivalent platforms).
Martech and tool agility: Hands-on experience or fast adaptability with enterprise Martech stacks (e.g. Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud), digital behavioral tools (e.g. Mouseflow), and AI productivity tools (e.g. Gemini, Glean).
Test and learn mindset: Practical experience setting up MVPs, building hypotheses, and running A/B tests to optimize digital experiences.
Project ownership and communication: Strong project management skills to drive initiatives independently in complex environments, paired with excellent written and verbal stakeholder communication.

What Success Looks Like

Effective content direction: Establishes strong alignment with content managers and writers, delivering clear, data-driven briefs that guide the creation and optimization of task-enabling help content.
Optimized AI knowledge inputs: Collaborates effectively with Platform Experience and Content Experience to enhance knowledge base input, driving measurable quality improvements in virtual agent responses.

Validated journey insights: Collaborates with platform and analytics teams to test and validate in-product measurement frameworks, translating data into actionable project priorities.
Efficient delivery: Project milestones and experiments are executed independently, on time, and backed by clear data-driven results, while maintaining clear communication, strong alignment, and momentum across stakeholder groups.

We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts.

Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us.

Taking ownership and driving impact 
Being open to change and feedback

About The Role And Team

As our Security Tech Lead Manager, you’ll manage a team of 2–3 security engineers within Platform Engineering and remain hands-on. You’ll own the security engineering roadmap and take responsibility for the team’s delivery, performance and development. Working with Product and Platform Engineering, you’ll help protect our marketplace, our customers and their data.

Our platform runs on Google Cloud and Kubernetes. You’ll focus on application and cloud security, secure software delivery and risks in internal and AI-enabled systems. You’ll turn security priorities into engineering work, make clear trade-offs and help teams adopt controls that fit their everyday workflows.

What You Will Do

Manage and develop the security team through regular one-to-ones, timely feedback, performance reviews and career development. Address underperformance and support hiring and onboarding.
Own the security engineering roadmap. Prioritise work based on risk, business needs and team capacity, delegate effectively and remove blockers to delivery.
Stay hands-on by building security controls and automation, reviewing code and guiding technical decisions across applications, cloud infrastructure and software delivery.
Partner with Product and Platform Engineering early in design. Lead threat modelling and security reviews, and help teams choose secure approaches that are practical to implement.
Improve vulnerability management. Assess findings in the context of exposure and business impact, agree remediation priorities with system owners and track issues through resolution.
Improve security checks in CI/CD and infrastructure as code, including dependency and secret scanning. Reduce false positives and help engineers act on findings.
Coordinate the security team’s technical contribution to incident response and investigations. Turn lessons from incidents into improvements to detection, response and preventive controls.
Work with Legal, IT and Trust & Safety on security controls, policies and audit evidence where responsibilities overlap.
Measure and communicate progress through remediation times, control coverage and adoption. Explain remaining risks, delivery progress and trade-offs to technical and business stakeholders.

Who You Are

You have substantial hands-on security engineering experience in a software or cloud environment and have implemented and operated security capabilities in production.
You have previously managed engineers as direct reports, including performance reviews, career development and difficult feedback. You can balance people management with technical contribution.
You have owned a security roadmap or programme, translated priorities into deliverable work and coordinated implementation across engineering teams.
You have strong knowledge of application and cloud security, including identity and access management, secrets management and secure software development.
You are experienced in threat modelling, secure code and design reviews, vulnerability prioritisation and practical incident response.
You can develop or automate in Ruby, Python, Go or a similar language, are comfortable reviewing backend code and have integrated security controls into engineering workflows.
You communicate clearly with engineers and non-technical partners, explain risk in business terms and gain support for decisions when priorities compete.

Helpful Experience

Experience with Google Cloud, Kubernetes and Terraform or similar infrastructure tooling.
Experience in a marketplace, e-commerce or another software product business, including account and API security.
Experience securing AI-enabled applications, agents or data pipelines, or using AI to improve security engineering workflows.

Why You'll Love Working with Us

Create a visible impact by working at scale in a global organisation serving millions of customers across 80+ categories. In our flat structure, every role has a broad scope and directly impacts both our customers and the business.
Learn and grow through our Learning & Development initiatives, including clear development plans and mentorship programmes to support your career progression.
A culture of connection defines us. We’re a passionate, diverse team of 800+ Catawikians representing 60+ nationalities. We foster an inclusive and queer-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to bring their full self to work.
Celebrate life’s moments with us. You’ll receive a €100 Catavoucher when you join, a €50 Catavoucher on your birthday, and an extra day off each year to “Pursue Your Passion”. We also offer additional leave for key work anniversaries and important life events. Benefits may vary by location.

Our Offices and Way of Working

Our vibrant offices in Amsterdam and Lisbon are designed to inspire collaboration. Most Catawikians operate in a hybrid setup, combining office-based and remote work, with a minimum of two days per week in the office, unless a role is explicitly stated as fully remote or fully office-based.
